questions.text: Let T be a full binary tree with 8 leaves. (A full binary tree has every level full.) Suppose two leaves a and b of T are chosen uniformly and independently at random. The expected value of the distance between a and b in T (i.e., the number of edges in the unique path between a and b) is (rounded off to 2 decimal places) ___________ .
questions.solution:
8 leaves, height 3. Fix leaf a; b is uniform over the 8 leaves (b can equal a):
- same leaf: distance 0 (1 leaf)
- sibling: distance 2 (1 leaf)
- same subtree of height 2: distance 4 (2 leaves)
- other half: distance 6 (4 leaves)

[latex]E=\frac{0+2+2\times4+4\times6}{8}=\frac{34}{8}=4.25[/latex]

Answer: 4.25

questions.text: Suppose Y is distributed uniformly in the open interval (1,6). The probability that the polynomial [latex]3x^2+6xY+3Y+6[/latex] has only real roots is (rounded off to 1 decimal place) _________.
questions.solution:
Real roots need discriminant [latex]\ge0[/latex]:
[latex](6Y)^2-4\cdot3\cdot(3Y+6)\ge0\Rightarrow36Y^2-36Y-72\ge0\Rightarrow(Y-2)(Y+1)\ge0[/latex]

For Y in (1, 6) this means [latex]Y\ge2[/latex]. Probability [latex]=\frac{6-2}{6-1}=\frac45=0.8[/latex]

Answer: 0.8

questions.text: Let [latex]\Sigma[/latex] be the set of all bijections from {1,...,5} to {1,...,5}, where [latex]id[/latex] denotes the identity function, i.e. [latex]id(j)=j,\forall j[/latex]. Let [latex]\circ[/latex] denote composition on functions. For a string [latex]x = x_1x_2 ... x_n \in \Sigma ^n, n \geq 0[/latex], let [latex]\pi(x) = x_1\circ x_2\circ ... \circ x_n[/latex]. Consider the language [latex]L = \{x \in \Sigma ^* | \pi(x) = id\}[/latex]. The minimum number of states in any DFA accepting L is _________ .
questions.solution:
The DFA only needs to remember the composition read so far, which is one of the [latex]5!=120[/latex] permutations of {1, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 5}. The start (and only final) state is id.

All 120 states are distinguishable: from state [latex]\sigma[/latex], reading [latex]\sigma^{-1}[/latex] leads to id, and that symbol leads to id from no other state. So the minimum is 120.

Answer: 120

questions.text: Consider that 15 machines need to be connected in a LAN using 8-port Ethernet switches. Assume that these switches do not have any separate up link ports. The minimum number of switches needed is ___________.
questions.solution:
Connecting switches uses ports (one port on each side of each link).
- 2 switches: 16 ports [latex]-[/latex] 2 for the link = 14 [latex]\lt[/latex] 15 False
- 3 switches in a chain: 24 ports [latex]-[/latex] 4 for 2 links = 20 [latex]\ge[/latex] 15 True

Answer: 3

questions.text: What is the minimum number of 2-input NOR gates required to implement 4-variable function expressed in sum-of-minterms from as [latex]f = \Sigma (0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15)[/latex]? Assume that all the inputs and their complements are available. Answer ________ .
questions.solution:
K-map: minterms 0, 2, 8, 10 = [latex]\bar B\bar D[/latex] and 5, 7, 13, 15 = BD. So [latex]f=BD+\bar B\bar D[/latex] (XNOR of B and D).

In product-of-sums form: [latex]f=(B+\bar D)(\bar B+D)[/latex]. With NOR gates:
- [latex]G_1=NOR(B,\bar D)[/latex], [latex]G_2=NOR(\bar B,D)[/latex]
- [latex]f=NOR(G_1,G_2)=(B+\bar D)(\bar B+D)[/latex]

3 gates (complements are available).

Answer: 3
